- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.62), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 1–3 day horizon after a spike; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for immediate follow-up.  
- Model overestimates in the 5–10 day horizon after a sharp rise; apply 1–3% downward correction to avoid overhang.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +/– 0.5+), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to capture momentum.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after 60+ days of rise), model often fails to correct; apply 0.5–1.5% downward bias for 3–5 day horizon.  
- If model forecast is > 2% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.3), model often misses trend; use 0.2–0.5% upward bias to capture latent momentum.
